informal: I wanna go to the mall cos I need to buy some stuff.
formal: I would like to go to the mall because I need to buy a few things.
focus: wanna → would like to; cos → because

informal: Yeah, she's kinda busy right now.
formal: Yes, she is rather busy at the moment.
focus: kinda → rather; right now → at the moment

informal: Can you gimme a hand with this?
formal: Could you help me with this, please?

informal: He was like, super tired, so he went home early.
formal: He was extremely tired, so he went home early.

informal: It's gonna rain later, for sure.
formal: It is going to rain later, most likely.
focus: gonna → going to; for sure → most likely

informal: I dunno what he wants from me.
formal: I do not know what he wants from me.

informal: That movie was hella boring ngl.
formal: That film was extremely boring, to be honest.
focus: hella → extremely; ngl → to be honest

informal: She's got a lotta stuff to do today.
formal: She has a great deal of work to do today.
focus: got → has; a lotta stuff → a great deal of work

informal: Me and my friend goes to the gym on Mondays.
formal: My friend and I go to the gym on Mondays.
focus: Me and my friend → My friend and I; goes → go

informal: It don't matter anyway.
formal: It does not matter anyway.

informal: We should of left earlier.
formal: We should have left earlier.

informal: He done really good on the test.
formal: He did really well on the test.

informal: There's like a billion people at the sale.
formal: There was an enormous crowd at the sale.
focus: a billion → an enormous crowd; like → (remove)

informal: I'm not really that into sports tbh.
formal: I am not particularly interested in sports, to be honest.
focus: into → interested in; tbh → to be honest

informal: Let me know ASAP cos the boss wants it.
formal: Please inform me as soon as possible, because the manager requires it.
focus: ASAP → as soon as possible; boss wants it → manager requires it

informal: This thing is way more better than the old one.
formal: This one is far better than the previous model.

informal: We was chilling at his place all weekend.
formal: We spent the weekend relaxing at his home.

informal: IDK, maybe just do whatever you want.
formal: I am not sure; perhaps you should do whatever you prefer.

informal: The teacher ain't gonna like this.
formal: The teacher will not be pleased with this.

informal: I could care less about the result.
formal: I could not care less about the result.
focus: could care less → could not care less (the idiom needs the 'not')

informal: She's the one what told me about it.
formal: She is the one who told me about it.

informal: We gotta hurry up or we'll miss the bus.
formal: We have to hurry, or we will miss the bus.

informal: It's basically the same thing, pretty much.
formal: It is essentially the same thing.

informal: He's hella smart but kinda lazy too.
formal: He is very intelligent but somewhat lazy as well.

informal: I'm good, thanks. You?
formal: I am well, thank you. And you?

informal: They was arguing about money and stuff.
formal: They were arguing about money and other matters.

informal: Gonna grab some food, wanna come?
formal: I am going to get some food. Would you like to join me?
focus: grab → get; wanna come → would you like to join me

informal: That's probs the best option ngl.
formal: That is probably the best option, to be honest.
focus: probs → probably; ngl → to be honest

informal: She don't really like him no more.
formal: She does not like him any more.
focus: don't → does not; no more → any more (double negative removed)

informal: Me and him was talking about you.
formal: He and I were talking about you.
focus: Me and him → He and I; was → were
